Name: supervised_probe_comparison
Title: Linear vs Nonlinear Probes: What Supervised Classifiers Reveal About Functional Information in Evo2 Embeddings
Experiment: Load cached embeddings from run_0/data/embeddings_evo2_7b.npy and labels from run_0/data/dataset.json. Train and compare three supervised probes on identical stratified train/test splits: (1) Logistic Regression (L2), (2) SVM (RBF kernel), (3) MLP (existing baseline). Report AUROC, accuracy, and F1 for each. Compute the nonlinearity gap (MLP AUROC - LR AUROC) to quantify how much nonlinear structure the embeddings contain. Perform 5-fold cross-validation for all models and report mean ± std AUROC. Generate a ROC curve plot comparing all three models.

Name: feature_importance_learning_curves
Title: What Drives Supervised Separability? Feature Importance and Learning Dynamics in Evo2 Embeddings
Experiment: Load cached embeddings and labels from run_0/data/. (1) Train baseline MLP and logistic regression classifiers on full training set. (2) Permutation feature importance: for the trained LR model, randomly shuffle each embedding dimension independently on the test set and measure AUROC drop; identify and visualize top-20 most important dimensions. (3) Per-dimension statistical analysis: compute Cohen's d effect size and two-sample KS statistic for each embedding dimension between the two functional classes; create ranked bar plots. (4) Learning curves: train LR and MLP classifiers on varying training set sizes (10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) with 5-fold cross-validation at each size; plot mean AUROC ± std vs. training size to assess sample efficiency and generalization. (5) PCA visualization: project embeddings to first 2 principal components, plot scatter colored by true labels, and overlay the linear decision boundary from the trained LR classifier using a meshgrid. (6) Unsupervised baseline: perform k-means clustering (k=2) on embeddings and compute adjusted rand index (ARI) and purity score against true labels; compare to supervised AUROC to quantify supervision benefit. Save all metrics as JSON and generate matplotlib figures (permutation importance bar plot, effect size distribution, learning curves, PCA projection with boundary, unsupervised vs supervised comparison).

Name: decision_boundary_geometry
Title: Geometric Analysis of Decision Boundaries: Confidence Landscapes and Boundary Structure in Evo2 Functional Embeddings
Experiment: Load cached embeddings and labels from run_0/data/. (1) Train three classifiers on identical stratified 80/20 splits with fixed seed: Logistic Regression (L2, C=1.0), SVM (RBF kernel, C=1.0, gamma='scale', probability=True), and MLP baseline (existing architecture). (2) Confidence analysis: For each model, extract prediction probabilities on test set. Compute confidence scores as |probability - 0.5| for LR/MLP and use decision_function for SVM margins. Identify high-confidence genes (top 25% by confidence) and low-confidence genes (bottom 25% by confidence) for each model. Compute overlap statistics: how many genes are consistently high/low confidence across all three models vs. model-specific. Save gene symbols for each category. (3) Embedding space interpolation: Compute class centroids (mean embedding vector) for DNA repair and TSG classes. Sample 50 evenly-spaced points along the linear interpolation path between centroids. For each interpolation point, compute predictions and confidence from all three models. Plot three curves (one per model) showing how prediction probability changes along the interpolation path. (4) 2D PCA visualization with decision boundaries: Project all embeddings to first 2 principal components. Create a dense meshgrid (100x100) over the PC space. For each grid point, compute predictions from all three models. Generate three subplots showing: (a) LR decision boundary as contour with confidence heatmap, (b) SVM-RBF boundary and heatmap, (c) MLP boundary and heatmap. Overlay test points colored by true labels. (5) Margin distribution analysis: Plot histograms of confidence scores for each model, separated by true class. Compute and report mean confidence for correctly vs. incorrectly classified samples. Perform t-test to assess whether misclassified genes have significantly lower confidence than correctly classified genes. Output all results as JSON (confidence statistics, gene lists, overlap metrics, mean confidence by correctness) and generate matplotlib figures (interpolation curves showing all three models, 3-panel PCA boundary visualization with heatmaps, confidence histogram comparison across models).

Name: intrinsic_dimensionality_analysis
Title: Intrinsic Dimensionality of Functional Information: How Many Dimensions Separate DNA Repair from Tumor Suppressor Genes?
Experiment: Load cached embeddings (8192-dim) and labels from run_0/data/. (1) Dimensionality and information content: Fit PCA on all embeddings using sklearn.decomposition.PCA. Plot cumulative explained variance ratio vs number of components (up to 500). Compute participation ratio as (sum of eigenvalues)^2 / sum of squared eigenvalues to estimate effective dimensionality. Report number of components needed for 50%, 90%, 95%, 99% variance. (2) Classification performance vs dimensionality: Project embeddings to k=[2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000] PCA dimensions. For each k, perform 5-fold stratified cross-validation with LogisticRegression(penalty='l2', C=1.0, max_iter=1000, random_state=0). Plot mean AUROC ± std vs k to identify minimum dimensions preserving functional separability. Visually identify the 'elbow' point where AUROC saturates. (3) Nonlinear manifold comparison (optional if umap-learn available): Apply UMAP(n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.1, random_state=0) to reduce embeddings to k=[2, 10, 50] dimensions. Train LogisticRegression with 5-fold CV on UMAP projections and compare AUROC to PCA at same k values. Generate side-by-side 2D scatter plots (PCA vs UMAP, both k=2) colored by true class labels. If UMAP unavailable, skip this analysis. (4) Supervised vs unsupervised reduction: Apply LinearDiscriminantAnalysis(n_components=1) from sklearn.discriminant_analysis and extract 1D projections. Train LogisticRegression on LDA projection and compare AUROC to first PCA component using 5-fold CV. This quantifies benefit of supervised dimensionality reduction. (5) Component-wise class separation: For top-5 principal components, create box plots showing PC score distributions separated by functional class. Compute Cohen's d effect size (mean difference / pooled std) for each PC to quantify which components most strongly separate the two classes. Output JSON with all metrics (explained variance thresholds, participation ratio, AUROC vs k for PCA/UMAP/LDA, Cohen's d per PC) and generate matplotlib figures (cumulative variance curve, AUROC vs dimensionality line plot with error bars, 2-panel 2D scatter if UMAP available, box plots for top-5 PCs grouped by class).
